ranked_candidates.hypothesis: CIL's aggressive renewable energy targets (9.5 GW by FY 2029-30) face potential execution risks when comparing announced project pipeline status against current commissioning rates (e.g., only 200 MW commissioned of the 300 MW Khavda project as of July 2026).
ranked_candidates.financial_importance: The transition represents a strategic pivot to diversify revenue streams. Failure to meet capacity targets may impair future growth valuations and sustainability narrative credibility.
metrics_and_periods: Progress status of 1.5 GW wind and 3 GW solar projects
Capex allocated for renewable energy projects

evidence_found.statement: Company targets 9.5 GW renewable energy capacity by FY 2029-30. Includes specific projects: 875 MW Pugal Solar, 80 MW/320 MWh BESS Odisha, 600 MW Jalaun Solar, 300 MW Khavda (200 MW commissioned July 2026).

additional_evidence_needed: Project-level completion timelines from external energy regulatory filings

data_risks_and_limitations: Reliance on internal management disclosure for project status; potential for over-optimistic project milestones.
